title: Stream 1: opencode_transport crate + backend skeleton + selector wiring
description:
Foundational stream that unblocks Streams 2 and 3.

Deliverables:
- New crate crates/opencode_transport/ with: process supervisor (lazy-start, backoff, kill-on-quit), HTTP client, SSE /event subscription with sessionID demuxer, JSON-RPC server framing for plugin -> Warp calls, vendored opencode wire schemas.
- New module app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/ skeleton: backend handle, session_router (reuse per-conversation session), event_to_client_action (first pass of SSE -> AIClientAction conversion), placeholder rpc_handlers (real handlers come in Stream 2), placeholder action_adapter, prompt_builder, persistence_glue stubs.
- FeatureFlag::UseOpencodeAsPrimaryAgent added to DEBUG_FLAGS in crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs.
- Selector wired in app/src/ai/agent/api/impl.rs so generate_multi_agent_output dispatches to either legacy warp_multi_agent_api or new opencode backend based on the flag (and backend_kind once Stream 3 lands).

Constraints:
- server_conversation_token MUST stay Warp-cloud only.
- Use crates/jsonrpc and crates/ipc where applicable for RPC framing.
- Use command::r#async::Command (NOT std::process::Command or async_process::Command).
- Use instant::Instant (NOT std::time::Instant).
- Tracing for logs; never dbg!.
- All new public modules in app/src/lib.rs are FORBIDDEN — wire through existing module tree.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/opencode_transport/ builds cleanly under cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/ skeleton compiles
- FeatureFlag::UseOpencodeAsPrimaryAgent appears in DEBUG_FLAGS and is accessible via .is_enabled()
- generate_multi_agent_output has a documented selector branch (legacy vs opencode); opencode branch may return a TODO!() / unimplemented stub at this point
- ./script/presubmit passes
- Unit tests for transport components (process supervisor lifecycle, SSE demuxer routes by sessionID) using App::test or pure unit tests

title: OpenCode as Primary Agent
description:
Replace the embedded warp_multi_agent_api backend with the open-source opencode runtime, gated behind FeatureFlag::UseOpencodeAsPrimaryAgent. See specs/opencode-as-primary-agent/TECH.md for the full design.

Three parallel work streams:
- Stream 1: opencode_transport crate + opencode_backend skeleton + feature flag + selector wiring (UNBLOCKS others)
- Stream 2: Bun TypeScript plugin + RPC handlers + parked-tool state machine
- Stream 3: persistence (backend_kind/opencode_session_id/opencode_id_map JSON fields) + bd prime memory injection + cancellation/abort plumbing

Phase 1 allowed tools: bash, read, edit, write, patch, glob, grep. Disabled: webfetch, todo, task, fetch, search, code, skill, lsp, plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- New conversations created with FeatureFlag::UseOpencodeAsPrimaryAgent enabled use opencode runtime end-to-end
- Existing Warp-cloud conversations continue working unchanged (backend_kind sticky)
- All Phase 1 allowlisted tools (bash/read/edit/write/patch/glob/grep) execute via Warp's ActionModel::queue_actions pipeline (preprocessing, approval, denylist, autoexecute all behave identically to legacy backend)
- Cancellation works: user cancel + subprocess crash both leave UI in usable state
- bd prime injection refreshes per-conversation on app start + every 30 min
- Feature flag in DEBUG_FLAGS; ready to be promoted to DOGFOOD_FLAGS once stable

title: Implement opencode_transport::http_client
description:
Thin reqwest-based wrapper for opencode HTTP API. Methods needed for Phase 1:

- POST /session — create session
- POST /session/:id/message — submit prompt
- POST /session/:id/abort — cancel turn
- POST /session/:id/tool/:call_id/response — submit RPC tool result back to opencode (after Warp executes the action)
- GET /session/:id — fetch session state (recovery)

Use reqwest with rustls feature. Vendored opencode wire schemas live in opencode_transport::schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each endpoint has typed request/response structs
- Errors map to a transport-level OpencodeApiError enum (network vs HTTP status vs deserialization)
- Unit tests use a wiremock or hyper fake server to round-trip each endpoint
- No std::time::Instant usage
- cargo clippy passes

title: Implement opencode_transport::sse_demuxer
description:
One global SSE /event subscription on the supervisor's endpoint. Demuxer routes events to per-session async channels keyed by sessionID extracted from each event payload.

API sketch:
- pub struct SseDemuxer { ... }
- impl SseDemuxer { pub fn new(http_endpoint: HttpEndpoint) -> Self; pub fn subscribe(&self, session_id: SessionId) -> Receiver<OpencodeEvent>; pub fn unsubscribe(&self, session_id: &SessionId); }
- Use async-broadcast or tokio::sync::broadcast for fan-in -> per-session unbounded mpsc.
- Reconnect on disconnect with backoff.
- Use instant::Instant if any timing logic, NOT std::time::Instant.
acceptance_criteria:
- Single SSE /event subscription regardless of number of subscribers
- Events with sessionID 'abc' are delivered only to subscribers of 'abc'
- Events without sessionID are logged and dropped (or routed to a sentinel channel)
- Reconnect on transport error with backoff; subscribers do not lose their channel during reconnect
- Unit test: feed synthetic JSON events into a fake source, assert routing
- cargo clippy passes

title: Implement opencode_transport::process_supervisor
description:
Lazy-start opencode serve subprocess per Warp app, supervised with backoff, killed on Warp quit. One subprocess shared by all conversations.

Use command::r#async::Command (NOT std::process::Command or async_process::Command — banned in .clippy.toml).

API sketch:
- pub struct Supervisor { ... }
- impl Supervisor { pub fn new(opencode_bin: PathBuf) -> Self; pub async fn ensure_running(&self) -> Result<HttpEndpoint>; pub async fn shutdown(&self); }
- HttpEndpoint = base URL of /event SSE + /session HTTP API.
- Backoff: exponential 100ms -> 5s, capped.
acceptance_criteria:
- Supervisor lazy-starts on first ensure_running()
- Subsequent ensure_running calls return cached endpoint
- shutdown() kills subprocess cleanly
- Subprocess crash triggers restart with exponential backoff
- Tracing emitted for: spawn, ready (port detected), exit, restart
- Unit test using a fake binary or short-lived shell script verifies lifecycle
- Uses command::r#async::Command exclusively
- cargo clippy passes

title: Stream 3: persistence + bd prime injection + cancellation plumbing
description:
Persistence and integration concerns. Can land in parallel with Stream 2 once Stream 1 selector is wired.

Deliverables:
- app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/persistence_glue.rs:
  - Add new fields to AgentConversationData JSON blob:
    - backend_kind: enum { Legacy, Opencode } (sticky per conversation; set at creation time based on FeatureFlag::UseOpencodeAsPrimaryAgent).
    - opencode_session_id: Option<String>.
    - opencode_id_map: { message_ids: HashMap<...>, part_ids: HashMap<...>, call_ids: HashMap<...> }.
  - JSON blob field — NO schema migration. Forward/backward compatible with serde defaults.
- app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/beads_glue.rs — bd prime read-only memory injection:
  - Cached per-conversation, refreshed on app start + every 30 min.
  - Missing bd binary -> tracing::warn + skip silently.
  - Read-only: never invokes bd writes.
  - Injected as system-prompt addendum via prompt_builder.rs.
- Cancellation/abort plumbing:
  - User cancel -> POST /session/:id/abort + park cancellation locally; UI returns to prompt.
  - Subprocess crash -> all parked calls -> SubprocessLost; user sees 'interrupted; try again' surface.
  - In-flight turns intentionally do NOT survive subprocess restart (documented behavior).

Constraints:
- backend_kind is sticky per conversation. Existing conversations created before feature flag stay on Legacy backend forever even if flag flips.
- New conversations evaluate the flag once at creation; subsequent flag toggles do not migrate them.
acceptance_criteria:
- AgentConversationData round-trips backend_kind/opencode_session_id/opencode_id_map through SQLite without schema migration.
- Existing conversations (without these fields in JSON) deserialize cleanly with backend_kind defaulting to Legacy.
- bd prime injection refreshes on app start + every 30 min (verifiable via tracing or test hook).
- Missing bd binary logs warn + does not crash.
- User-cancel during opencode turn returns UI to prompt, leaves conversation usable.
- Subprocess kill mid-turn -> all parked calls transition to SubprocessLost, UI surfaces 'interrupted'.

title: Stream 2: opencode plugin + RPC handlers + parked-tool state machine
description:
Long-pole stream. Bridges opencode tool calls to Warp's ActionModel pipeline so user-facing semantics (preprocessing, approval, denylist, autoexecute, cancellation) match the legacy backend.

Deliverables:
- resources/opencode-plugin/ — Bun TypeScript plugin that:
  - At init, enumerates ALL opencode built-ins via ctx.client.tools.list({source:'builtin'}).
  - SHADOWS every built-in with a registered tool of the same name.
  - For names in allowlist [bash, read, edit, write, patch, glob, grep] -> forwards to Warp via JSON-RPC over stdio (or local socket).
  - For everything else -> returns a structured 'disabled-tool' error.
  - Belt-and-braces opencode permission config also denies non-allowlisted names.
- app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/rpc_handlers.rs — real handlers for the 7 allowlisted tools that go through ActionModel::queue_actions(...) (NOT try_to_execute_action directly).
- ParkedToolCall state machine in app/src/ai/agent/opencode_backend/parked_call.rs:
  - States: Submitted -> AwaitingPreprocess -> AwaitingApproval -> Approved -> Executing -> {Completed, Cancelled, Failed, SubprocessLost}.
  - Dedupe SSE-side tool result against RPC-side result by opencode_call_id; SSE result arriving means shadowing leaked -> tracing::warn.
- action_adapter.rs converts each allowlisted opencode tool input into the corresponding AIAgentAction variant.

Constraints:
- Vendor opencode tool schemas alongside the plugin (do not fetch at runtime).
- Plugin is bundled as a resource; spawned by the process supervisor from Stream 1.
- All seven Phase 1 tools must round-trip through preprocessing + approval gates exactly like legacy.
acceptance_criteria:
- resources/opencode-plugin/ builds with bun (or whatever runner the plugin uses) and is bundle-shipped.
- Plugin enumerates and shadows built-ins on init; non-allowlisted shadows return structured errors.
- All 7 allowlisted tools (bash/read/edit/write/patch/glob/grep) execute via ActionModel::queue_actions; preprocessing + approval + denylist + autoexecute + cancellation flows behave identically to legacy backend (verified by integration test).
- ParkedToolCall transitions are unit-tested for every state edge incl. SubprocessLost.
- Dedupe path logs tracing::warn when SSE result arrives for an RPC-handled call.
